full_judgment: 28. We are fully agreed with the said principle of law enunciated in the said cases. Now, question is how far these are applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. Each case has its own merit and principle of law should not be applied mechanically, rather it should be applied considering the facts and circumstances and it's own merit. In the instant case we have examined exhibit 1, the seizure list vis-a-vis the evidence of PW 7, the informant and PW 8 the investigating officer. It appears to us that subsequently the words “কোমরে গোজা অবস্থায়” was inserted in the column of the seizure list and PW 7 Mahbubur Rahman, the informant admitted in his cross-examination that there was no 'initial' on the said portion of seizure list, which creates a presumption that the “কোমরে গোজা অবস্থায়” has been inserted subsequently in the seizure list and same was after thought act of police. The defence further put suggestion specifically to the investigating officer that the alleged arms were not in order. PW 8 the investigating officer in his cross-examination admitted that he did not send the arms to the expert for examination. This also creates a doubt as to the position of the arms, whether it was in order. To convict a person under section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act, the alleged arms must be a firearms and workable one.
